punchline: Executives expected their underwriters to differ by about 10 percent on the same case, and the gap was 55 percent.
thirty_sec: An insurer gave forty-eight underwriters the same realistic case summaries and asked each for a premium. Executives expected about a 10 percent difference between any two. The typical gap was 55 percent of the average premium, more than five times that. Kahneman, Sibony and Sunstein call it noise: the file was identical, only the person changed.
